units.function: Removes a managed Paperclip CLI installation while attempting to preserve instance data, unregister the current background service, avoid disrupting other named instances and refuse deletion of an unverified install store.
units.dependencyDirection: uninstall command -> instance/home configuration, service-manager detection and Paperclip-specific install-store mutation helpers -> host filesystem, shell startup files and launchd/systemd definitions. It is an operator CLI lifecycle command, not a domain or service API.

units.testAssessment: The already-audited managed-install test unit covers successful uninstall with user-data preservation, other-instance refusal, unavailable-systemd refusal, unverified-store refusal and lock contention. Those are useful focused safety cases. It does not prove transactionality across service/store removal, concurrent creation of another instance definition, Darwin manager-unavailable behavior, injected-home consistency, crash recovery, audit evidence or real launchd/systemd integration.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted/local-enterprise deployments need safe, reversible component removal and upgrade ceremonies that never confuse program files, configuration, credentials, evidence or business data and that account for multiple profiles/nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the verified-ownership marker, no-follow path validation, mutation lock, shared-instance check and explicit data-preservation contract into a Company OS deployment manager. units.responsibilityConflict: The destructive operation is authorized only by local process access. It has no accountable human, approved removal plan/digest, reason, affected Connector/runtime inventory, evidence record or retention disposition; service removal and filesystem deletion are not one recoverable change transaction.
evidence: Existing completed cli/src/__tests__/install-command.test.ts evidence reused: successful data-preserving uninstall, other-instance refusal, unavailable-systemd refusal, unverified-store refusal and lock contention
units.securityFindings: Positive controls include explicit managed-store ownership verification before recursive deletion, a second verification inside the lock, refusal to remove a shared shim while other instance definitions exist, and preservation of product data. Residual risks: the service is uninstalled before the store lock, so a later lock/verification/delete failure leaves a partial state; the other-instance scan occurs outside the lock and can race; the injected userHomeDir is used for service scanning while resolveInstallStorePaths and RC edits use process-global environment, permitting inconsistent targets in embedding/tests; unsupported service-manager fail-closed logic is Linux-specific; RC edits and recursive store deletion have no durable journal or rollback; there is no plan/preview, confirmation, retention manifest or auditable actor/reason. A local attacker able to mutate service definitions or environment between checks may influence the operation, although install-store ownership guards constrain the deletion root.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL: worktree env prints all adjacent env entries as JSON or shell exports, including database URLs and signing/credential values. CRITICAL: seeding copies the local-encrypted master key and shared Agent JWT Secret alongside a database clone, reproducing decryptable Secrets and identity authority without a governed export/rebinding ceremony. HIGH: preserve-live-work can retain runnable assignments/timers and allow-live-target can overwrite a database while detected running; repair invokes destructive reseed/force paths with internal yes=true. HIGH: force cleanup can recursively delete a worktree, unique commits, uncommitted changes and instance data without an approved manifest or recovery journal. HIGH: attachment bodies are written to external storage inside a SQL transaction without size/SHA-256 verification or rollback, permitting orphaned/overwritten objects and DB/blob divergence. HIGH: preview/confirmation is not bound to source/target revisions or a content digest, and --yes bypasses it. MEDIUM: package installation executes fetched repository lifecycle scripts; Git hooks, including symlinks, are recursively copied into worktree Git state. MEDIUM: whole-company histories and blobs are buffered without pagination/limits; port allocation and several filesystem checks are check-then-act; fixed embedded PostgreSQL credentials rely solely on loopback/isolation; PID locks can wait indefinitely and stale cleanup is manual. Positive controls include tenant-prefixed normalized object keys, migration-state checks, seed locking, quarantining Agent execution, pausing schedules, stable-ID imports, atomic issue-counter reservation and explicit unsupported-run disclosure.

units.function: A deterministic in-memory planner for importing issues, comments, projects/workspaces, documents/revisions and attachments between Paperclip worktree databases. It preserves stable IDs where possible, reports drift/skips and explicitly clears missing Agent/project/goal references.
units.dependencyDirection: merge planner -> direct @paperclipai/db table inference types. The algorithm is otherwise pure, but is tightly coupled to Paperclip schema rows rather than a versioned portable transfer contract.
units.keyDataModels: WorktreeMergePlan; planned insert/skip/merge variants; import adjustments; issue/comment/document/revision/attachment/project/workspace database rows; target identity/reference sets; provisional issue/revision numbers.
units.lifecycle: Index target/source rows -> deterministically sort parents, timestamps and IDs -> classify stable-ID collisions and drift -> clear or map unavailable Agent/project/workspace/goal references -> renumber conflicting document revisions -> calculate counts/adjustments -> return a preview consumed by the imperative apply command.
units.testAssessment: The completed focused merge-history suite passed 8/8 and covers deterministic issue/comment/document/attachment planning, drift, project mapping/import and adjustment counts. It does not cover cyclic/dangling parents, unknown scope tokens, missing human identities, source/target tenant mismatch, same-ID semantic conflicts, workspace command safety, document three-way conflicts, attachment asset/object collisions, schema evolution, large inputs or property-based idempotency.
units.designRationale: Separating a pure deterministic plan from side-effectful apply makes destructive transfer explainable and testable. Stable IDs allow repeat imports to skip known records; explicit adjustment counts surface lost Agent relationships; deterministic revision renumbering avoids simple numeric collisions.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explainable, repeatable migration/FDE template and environment promotion plans that preserve evidence provenance and responsibility while resolving identities, Connectors, data grants and executable workspace behavior explicitly.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure plan/apply separation, discriminated actions, deterministic ordering, stable-ID collision reporting and explicit adjustment ledger. Re-express it over Company OS versioned transfer DTOs, not database rows. Add three-way/base revisions, signed source/target snapshot digests, strict tenant and human/Agent identity mapping, responsibility/evidence dispositions, executable-field quarantine, fail-closed schema evolution and property/idempotency tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: Missing Agent attribution is silently nullified while human IDs are preserved without verifying that the same accountable principal exists in the target. Existing same-ID issues are skipped despite drift, and existing documents can be source-overwritten without an explicit conflict decision. The plan has no responsibility contract, approver, reason, evidence or data-authorization mapping.
evidence: Existing completed application:cli/__tests__/worktree-merge-history assessment reused: focused Vitest 8/8 passed
units.securityFindings: HIGH: createdBy/updatedBy/assignee user IDs are copied without confirming target-principal existence or equivalence, while missing Agent IDs are cleared; this can create dangling or falsely attributed human responsibility. HIGH: imported project workspaces carry cwd, repository, setupCommand, cleanupCommand and remote metadata without executable-field quarantine. HIGH: existing documents with matching UUID can be source-overwritten/merged without a base revision or explicit conflict policy; existing issues with drift are simply skipped, producing asymmetric silent divergence. MEDIUM: issue parent IDs are not validated against the target/import set and cycles are tolerated rather than rejected; target FK behavior becomes the accidental guard. MEDIUM: an input such as issues,unknown silently accepts issues because unknown scope tokens are discarded. MEDIUM: attachment planning checks attachment ID only, not asset ID/object-key/hash collisions. Direct database row types make future schema additions easy to omit silently. Positive properties include deterministic tie-breaks, explicit missing-reference adjustments, stable-ID deduplication, parent-first intent and isolated pure planning.

units.function: Applies a command-line data-root override by mutating process-global Paperclip home, instance, config and context environment variables according to the receiving command's declared option support.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI option helper -> shared home/instance path resolution -> process.env. It supplies ambient configuration to later commands rather than returning a complete immutable context.
units.keyDataModels: DataDirOptionLike, per-command support flags, PAPERCLIP_HOME/INSTANCE_ID/CONFIG/CONTEXT.
units.lifecycle: Trim/resolve data root -> mutate global home -> conditionally infer and set instance/config/context unless explicit flags or existing environment values win.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed data-dir evidence: focused Vitest passed 4/4 for basic layout/override behavior. Instance/path adversaries, canonicalization, symlinks, permissions, command-support drift, nested invocation and process-global collision are absent.
units.designRationale: A single compatibility flag can redirect legacy commands to another local instance without threading paths through every call.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS operators and local nodes need explicit profile-scoped configuration that cannot leak across concurrent tenants, instances, tests or embedded invocations.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as an immutable DeploymentContext returned by a single precedence resolver. Pass it explicitly through application and adapter boundaries; reserve environment mutation for a narrow process-launch adapter.
units.responsibilityConflict: Ambient mutation hides which deployment/tenant a destructive command targets and provides no target digest or accountable change context.
units.securityFindings: Process-global state permits cross-command and embedded-call target contamination. Existing environment values silently outrank data-dir-derived config/context, creating mixed-root configurations; support flags can drift from actual command behavior. No canonical root/symlink/ownership policy is enforced here.

units.function: Loads, reads, generates and preservation-merges Paperclip-owned dotenv entries, including the shared Agent JWT signing Secret.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI env helper -> shared env-file writer plus dotenv -> filesystem, CSPRNG and process.env. Identity signing material is coupled to ambient process configuration.
units.keyDataModels: PAPERCLIP_AGENT_JWT_SECRET; PAPERCLIP_* owned entries; adjacent .env file; process-wide loaded-file cache.
units.lifecycle: Resolve config-adjacent .env -> optionally load once into process.env without override -> read global or file Secret -> generate 256-bit hex Secret if absent -> atomically preservation-merge managed entries.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed Agent JWT env evidence: 6/6 passed for preservation and dotenv round trips. Permissions, symlinks, concurrent writers, multi-instance process behavior, rotation/revocation, JWT issuer/audience and compromise recovery are absent.
units.designRationale: Preserve operator-owned dotenv bytes while allowing managed keys to evolve; avoid repeatedly loading the same file and avoid overwriting explicit process values.
units.companyOsProblem: Each Company OS product, deployment, Connector and runtime needs isolated, rotatable signing/credential authority with stable configuration provenance and no cross-instance ambient leakage.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind SecretProvider and IdentityPort. Keep the preservation-aware atomic dotenv merger only for a local-development adapter; config-specific reads must read the requested source directly, and runtime keys require issuer/audience/scope/version/rotation/revocation metadata.
units.responsibilityConflict: A shared ambient signing Secret cannot establish which product/deployment issued an Agent credential or bind it to accountable human authority and independent audiences.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL: readAgentJwtSecretFromEnv(configPath) loads with override=false and then reads process.env, so a Secret loaded for the first instance can be returned for a later config path; ensureAgentJwtSecret may therefore skip creating the target instance key and share signing authority accidentally. Parse failures become an empty map without distinguishing corruption, and Secret reads trim values. The managed key filter and preservation-aware atomic writer are positive, but permissions/ownership/no-follow behavior is delegated and rotation does not exist.

units.function: Thin CLI wrappers around shared Paperclip home/instance path derivation, adding context/auth locations and a local-instance path summary.

units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Define a Company OS DeploymentLayoutPort and profile manifests; do not copy this branded facade or ambient instance semantics.

units.securityFindings: This wrapper adds little risk beyond ambient instance selection; permissions, ownership and canonical/no-follow enforcement are not represented in its return types. The shared implementation remains the canonical unit for path-validation judgment.

units.function: Normalizes one hostname-like input through the URL parser and parses a comma-separated deduplicated hostname list.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI parser -> platform URL implementation. It does not own runtime Host enforcement or proxy trust.
units.keyDataModels: Raw hostname/URL strings and normalized lowercase hostname arrays.
units.lifecycle: Trim -> add http scheme if absent -> URL parse -> return lowercase hostname -> preserve first-occurrence order while deduplicating CSV entries.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed allowed-hostname evidence: 1/1 passed for scheme/port/lowercase normalization and duplicates. Trailing dots, IDNA, IPv6, wildcard/subdomain policy, credentials, malformed/multiple Host headers, proxies and DNS rebinding are absent.
units.designRationale: Accept user-friendly host-or-URL input while storing only the authority hostname.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed and self-hosted profiles need explicit origin/host/proxy trust policies without confusing parsing normalization with authorization.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the URL-parser normalization as one stage inside a stricter HostPolicy value object with explicit IP/IPv6/IDNA/trailing-dot/wildcard semantics and runtime enforcement tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct responsibility conflict, but unsafe origin policy can expose approval and evidence interfaces to an unintended network authority.
units.securityFindings: The parser validates syntax, not trust. It does not distinguish exact hosts from wildcard policy, public DNS from local/IP literals, or direct Host from trusted proxy forwarding. Unknown URL components are discarded, which is convenient but can hide misleading user input; runtime guards must operate on canonical request authority independently.

units.function: Re-exports the complete shared Paperclip configuration schema, merge helpers, warnings and TypeScript types through the CLI source tree.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI schema facade -> relative ../../../packages/shared/src/config-schema.js source path. It bypasses a published package export boundary and contains no schema logic itself.
units.keyDataModels: PaperclipConfig and its database, server, auth, telemetry, update, storage, Secret and metadata sections.
units.lifecycle: Compile-time/runtime re-export only.
units.testAssessment: No behavior exists in this file; shared schema and config-store tests are separate units. TypeScript can catch symbol drift but not distribution/layout compatibility.
units.designRationale: Maintain historical CLI import paths while centralizing schema behavior in shared source.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a stable, versioned configuration contract consumable by CLI, services and deployment tooling without source-layout coupling.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT this source-relative facade. Publish a canonical Company OS config package/API with explicit compatibility versions and generated JSON Schema where external tooling needs it.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct domain conflict; the concern is ownership and upgrade stability of deployment policy.
units.securityFindings: A relative import into another package's src directory couples CLI builds to monorepo layout and can evade intended package export/version boundaries. Security behavior depends entirely on the separately audited shared schema.

units.function: Creates a local-encryption master-key file for the configured Secret provider unless an inline environment key or different provider is selected.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI Secret bootstrap -> config/path resolver -> process.env, filesystem and CSPRNG.
units.keyDataModels: Secret provider, configured/overridden key-file path, 32 random bytes encoded base64 and creation status.
units.lifecycle: Check provider -> prefer inline environment authority -> resolve override/config path -> accept any existing path -> otherwise mkdir and write a nominal 0600 key.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed Secret evidence: 8/8 passed for selected provider/bootstrap diagnostics and migration cases. This helper's race, symlink, type/owner/mode/content validation, real encryption, rotation and compromise recovery are unproved.
units.designRationale: Provide zero-configuration local Secret encryption with strong random key material and restrictive nominal permissions.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted Company OS needs pluggable key custody, explicit deployment ownership, rotation/versioning and safe bootstrap without accepting arbitrary existing files as trusted keys.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind a KeyProvider with exclusive no-follow creation, validated owner/type/mode/length, atomic rotation generations and recovery/escrow policy. Local files remain one adapter, not the product Secret model.
units.responsibilityConflict: Key creation has no deployment-claim actor, custody acknowledgment or recovery responsibility; possessing an ambient environment key silently establishes authority.
units.securityFindings: HIGH: existsSync followed by ordinary write is a check-then-act race and follows attacker-controlled symlinks; an existing directory, weak/empty file, wrong owner or permissive mode is accepted as a valid key. mkdir permissions are ambient. Entropy and intended 0600 mode are good, but chmod failure is ignored and no rotation/revocation/version metadata exists.

units.function: Builds quickstart server/auth configurations for loopback, LAN, tailnet or custom bind addresses and infers deployment/exposure defaults.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI server-profile composer -> shared bind predicates/constants -> optional tailscale subprocess and process environment. It creates policy-bearing config but does not enforce runtime request security.
units.keyDataModels: BindMode, DeploymentMode, DeploymentExposure, host/port/allowedHostnames, publicBaseUrl, signup setting and UI serving flag.
units.lifecycle: Resolve explicit bind/host/profile -> optionally detect a tailnet IPv4 -> choose host and deployment mode -> produce server and auth config with public-base mode.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed network-bind evidence: 5/5 passed for local_trusted loopback and missing-tailnet fallback. Authenticated/managed, LAN/custom, TLS/origin/proxy, adversarial addresses and runtime changes are not covered.
units.designRationale: Make secure local setup easy while offering explicit network exposure profiles and a safe loopback fallback when tailnet discovery fails.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs formally valid managed-cloud and local-enterprise network profiles where authentication, TLS/origin/proxy trust and signup/claim ceremonies cannot be composed into unsafe states.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a closed DeploymentProfile state machine validated both at configuration and runtime. Non-loopback must require authentication and an explicit origin/TLS/proxy policy; bootstrap signup/claim is a separate one-time ceremony and tailnet is only an adapter.
units.responsibilityConflict: An unsafe bind can expose responsibility approvals and evidence to unauthenticated actors; open signup also changes who may become a human principal without a deployment claim contract.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL: buildCustomServerConfig accepts deploymentMode=local_trusted with 0.0.0.0, a LAN address or arbitrary custom host; it only forces exposure metadata to private and does not force loopback/authentication. All generated auth configs set disableSignUp=false. Tailnet command output and explicit override are not validated as addresses, and a failed tailnet probe returns loopback while retaining tailnet bind semantics. Authenticated public mode can be composed with an undefined/unvalidated publicBaseUrl at this layer.

units.function: Discovers, reads, migrates, validates, extension-merges, backs up and durably atomically writes Paperclip JSON configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI config store -> schema/merge facade and home resolver -> synchronous filesystem, cwd/process environment and platform fsync behavior.
units.keyDataModels: PaperclipConfig, metadata-excluded effective equality, legacy pglite migration, invalid and rolling backup files.
units.lifecycle: Resolve override/env/ancestor/default path -> parse/migrate/schema-validate -> merge existing extensions -> no-op compare -> optionally bind invalid backup bytes -> durable backup -> exclusive temporary write, fsync, rename and directory fsync.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed config-store evidence: 3/3 passed and verifies durability ordering plus byte preservation. Ownership/modes, symlinks, concurrent revisions, disk failures, backup lifecycle/encryption, Secret redaction and ancestor trust are absent.
units.designRationale: Fail closed on invalid operator configuration, preserve extension fields during repairs, avoid needless writes and survive crashes with fsync plus rename.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs durable, versioned, extension-preserving deployment configuration with optimistic concurrency and clear ownership across cloud and local profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the exclusive temp/fsync/rename protocol, invalid-byte backup binding, no-op comparison and extension-preserving merge. Add canonical/no-follow paths, owner/mode policy, revision/CAS, bounded backups, redacted structured errors and explicit repository-config trust.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configuration mutations affecting identity, Connectors, data and execution are filesystem operations without actor/reason/approval evidence; higher layers must bind the validated diff to a change record.
units.securityFindings: Positive: exclusive 0600 temporary creation, file and directory fsync, atomic rename, durable backup and invalid-config byte equality are strong crash-safety patterns. HIGH: automatic ancestor discovery trusts repository .paperclip/config.json, which can redirect storage/database/network/runtime behavior when commands run in an untrusted checkout. MEDIUM: no lock/revision prevents concurrent lost updates; symlinked file/ancestor paths and owner/mode are not rejected; invalid-backup compare and final write remain a TOCTOU window; .backup is overwritten without retention/encryption; temporary-name retry is unbounded. Parse errors can include source-derived parser text and paths that callers may print.

units.function: The executable CLI composition root registering setup, deployment, identity, data, Agent, work, approval, Plugin, Connector-like, maintenance and worktree commands plus global pre-action context/env/telemetry hooks and top-level error handling.

No focused main/preAction/flush/error test proves mixed config precedence, invalid config, telemetry failure, signal handling, stable error codes, Secret argv exposure or every destructive command's effect classification.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a generated/thin operator CLI over stable APIs with explicit DeploymentContext, effect classes, machine-stable errors, accountable confirmations and no duplicate authority model.

evidence: Completed CLI parity/command evidence reused; CLI TypeScript passes
units.securityFindings: HIGH: --api-key accepts bearer material in process argv. HIGH: the global pre-action uses ambient mutable config/env, including the cross-instance Secret issue from the completed env audit. Errors are English strings with no stable code and may contain paths/source details. flushTelemetry failure can replace command outcome or escape the catch because it runs in finally; void main has no outer rejection handler. There is no signal-aware flush/cleanup. Broad static imports also make every Adapter/data/deployment capability part of one privileged operator process.

units.function: Route-level tests for Company activity, all-actor audit access tiers, Issue-run lookup, activity creation authorization and cross-tenant heartbeat-run existence-oracle resistance.

Missing are cursor behavior for the ordinary activity endpoint, stable structured error codes, malformed/oversized filters, field-level policy evolution, response schema contracts, actor spoofing on create, rate limiting, CSRF, audit of denied queries, full middleware integration and leakage through timing or related entity fields.

Define policy-versioned field projections, cursor pagination, structured error codes and immutable access receipts. Separate a broad operational activity stream from the narrowly authorized ResponsibilityLedger rather than redacting one row shape ad hoc.

The create surface is only shown checking Company access, not authority to assert the supplied actor/action/evidence semantics.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for ordered activity listing, compact Issue-run ledger projections and asynchronous liveness backfill from run-bound comments and document revisions.
units.dependencyDirection: ActivityService reads ActivityLog, HeartbeatRun, Issue, comment and document/revision relations; it normalizes provider-shaped usage/results for API projection and can persist derived liveness fields back onto completed heartbeat runs.
units.keyDataModels: ActivityLog timestamp/action, heartbeat run context/usage/result/liveness/continuation, Issue status, run-bound Issue comment, document revision createdByRunId and continuation-summary document key.
units.lifecycle: Company activity is returned newest first with a limit. Issue-run views omit context snapshots and normalize a small allowlist of token, cost, billing and timeout fields. Completed runs missing liveness are classified and persisted; same-run concrete comments or document revisions can establish progress, while other-run revisions and continuation summaries are excluded and plan-only text stays non-evidence.
units.testAssessment: Five database integration cases validate ordering, payload compaction, persistence of a completed classification and two important false-positive exclusions. Missing are cursor pagination, deterministic ordering on timestamp ties, currency/provider provenance, invalid/negative/overflow usage, redaction of secrets in allowed fields, concurrent backfill, failure retry, immutable source hashes, deleted/edited comments, artifact/evidence authorization, all liveness classes and proof that classification changes cannot rewrite historical accountability.
units.designRationale: Keep the Issue run ledger fast and bounded despite arbitrary provider payloads, and repair older or incomplete runs using concrete artifacts instead of trusting an Agent's prose summary as proof of progress.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs efficient run projections and a defensible separation between self-reported status, observable work activity, evidence artifacts and final responsibility records.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the allowlisted payload projection, exact run binding and exclusion of continuation summaries. Keep liveness as a recomputable operational projection with classifier version and source references. Evidence admission must instead create immutable, content-addressed Evidence records with origin, authorization, retention and verification state; cost needs currency, provider and pricing provenance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Backfilled liveness mutates the run record and labels comments/revisions as concrete action evidence without an immutable admission receipt or accountable reviewer. It is a useful health inference, not proof that the authorized goal was satisfied, the data use was permitted or the result was approved. Compact cost fields also lose enough provenance to be unsuitable for contractual accounting.

units.function: Route tests for explicit Adapter model-cache refresh and environment-aware suppression of local OpenCode discovery on remote execution environments.
units.dependencyDirection: The authenticated Agent route resolves Company access and Environment metadata, looks up a server Adapter, then invokes its listModels or refreshModels capability; OpenCode discovery is conditionally replaced by package fallback metadata.

Missing are explicit permission assertions for refresh, cross-Company environment IDs, nonexistent environments, refresh storms/rate limits, timeout/cancellation, cache scope by Company/credential/environment, stale/error metadata, structured error codes and disclosure of models unavailable to the selected execution/data policy.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must keep tenant governance separate from host code authority and enforce non-bypassable deployment-profile security floors across managed-cloud and self-hosted/local enterprise profiles.

Local enterprise can delegate package trust only through explicit policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single instance-admin boolean is too coarse for introducing executable supply-chain code and does not identify requester, approver and accountable operator separately. units.function: Route tests for validating Agent Adapter types and applying Codex-local credential/home isolation defaults during Agent create and update.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must let many vendor-neutral Connectors coexist without inheriting a developer's personal credentials, configuration, sessions or filesystem state, and must keep enterprise secrets and execution identities isolated by tenant and Connector instance.

units.function: Cryptographic unit tests for locally minted Agent run JWTs, including run/responsible-user/scope claims, expiry, issuer/audience validation, Company- and instance-derived keys and optional legacy master-secret verification.
units.dependencyDirection: The local runtime token helper reads process-level signing configuration, derives an HMAC key from control-plane instance and Company identifiers, signs Agent/run claims and verifies them before middleware constructs a request actor.
units.keyDataModels: Agent subject, Company, Adapter type, run id, responsible user, skill-test scope, instance id, issuer/audience, issued/expiry times and legacy-fallback policy.
units.lifecycle: Minted tokens default to a one-hour lifetime and are bound by claims and signature to one Company and control-plane instance. Missing signing configuration disables mint/verify. Issuer, audience, expiration, claim tampering and cross-instance use are rejected. A configurable compatibility path accepts tokens signed directly with the shared master secret; it can be disabled while derived-key tokens continue to work.
units.testAssessment: Sixteen focused cryptographic cases cover normal and scoped tokens, missing/fallback secrets, expiry, issuer/audience, Company and instance isolation, tampering, TTL and legacy-floor behavior. Missing are key identifiers/rotation overlap, asymmetric signing or KMS, jti/revocation, not-before/clock skew, algorithm-confusion/invalid JSON/oversize cases, claim schema validation, Agent/run lifecycle revocation, responsible-human status changes and proof that a token cannot cross deployment profile or Connector instance.
units.designRationale: Give local Agent processes short-lived delegated access without database lookup for every signature check, while limiting a shared secret's direct tenant/instance reach and preserving an upgrade path for already issued tokens.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs short-lived, audience-specific runtime attestations that let any Connector act only for an exact Work execution, tenant and approved responsibility/data contract across managed-cloud and local enterprise nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the tenant/instance key separation, narrow run scope and strict issuer/audience/expiry checks. Use a versioned RuntimeAttestation with key id, Connector instance, WorkExecution, ResponsibilityContract version, authorization/data-policy digest, jti and short expiry; support rotation and revocation through IdentityPort/KMS. Do not fall back to a human-login secret or tenant-agnostic master signature in production.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsible_user_id is a signed string captured at mint time, not evidence that the human accepted responsibility or remained authorized. The token omits approval, permission, data contract and evidence-policy versions. Legacy master-secret acceptance weakens both Company and instance isolation and can outlive organizational changes until expiry.

units.function: Route tests for cross-Company Agent lifecycle/key isolation and the guarded human action that clears an Agent error only when its organization chain is healthy.

Error recovery reads organization-chain health and appends an ActivityLog event after mutation.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, Company-scoped Agent, Agent API key and owning Agent id, Agent status/pause state, organization-chain health/reason/guidance and error-cleared audit action.
units.lifecycle: An outsider receives the same Agent-not-found 404 for pause, error clear, key list/create/revoke and no protected mutation runs. A Board user can clear an error Agent and emits a distinct audit action, but invalid reporting chains and non-error state return 409 without mutation or success audit.
units.testAssessment: Five route cases cover multiple cross-tenant operations, key-to-Agent ownership, principal type, successful recovery audit and two conflict conditions. Missing are real authz middleware/service integration because the authorization module is replaced, explicit permission variants, local_implicit blast radius, anonymous/instance-admin behavior, concurrent status changes, idempotency, active-run cancellation, key list content leakage, audit-write transaction failure, repair evidence and responsibility acceptance after recovery.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must hide tenant resources, bind every credential to the exact Agent/Connector instance and require a valid accountable-human chain before a failed Agent can resume effectful work.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the indistinguishable 404 pattern, deny-before-side-effect order, key ownership check, human-only recovery and organization-chain gate. Model recovery as a versioned command with expected Agent state, remediation reason/evidence, responsible human, optional risk-based approval, active-run disposition and immutable decision/result receipt. units.responsibilityConflict: The clear-error action proves only that a Board actor clicked recovery while the current org chain was syntactically valid. It does not show that the underlying failure was repaired, that the accountable human accepted resumed risk, or that permissions/data contracts and outstanding runs were revalidated. local_implicit access bypasses ordinary Company membership in the test helper.

units.keyDataModels: Managed/external bundle mode, root/managed-root/entry-file/file path, Company/Agent/instance identifiers, filtered file listing/export map, healed Adapter config and recovery warnings.

Listings/exports omit OS junk, Node dependencies and Python caches. If config is absent, partial or points at a stale root, an existing managed bundle wins and warnings explain the repair. Later writes/deletes return corrected metadata.
units.testAssessment: Eight useful filesystem cases cover both mode transitions, nested files, common junk filtering, missing/partial/stale metadata, entry recovery and write/delete healing. Missing are symlink/hardlink escape, ../ and absolute entry paths, root ownership/mode, maximum files/bytes/depth, atomic copy/rollback, concurrent writes, malicious encodings, Secret/PII scanning, executable content policy, content hashes/signatures, version history, approval/audit and behavior when both disk and database changed legitimately.
units.designRationale: Make instruction files portable between user-managed workspaces and a predictable Paperclip-owned location while tolerating older/stale configuration and keeping noisy dependency/cache trees out of API payloads.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reproducible, reviewable instruction artifacts that Connectors can materialize safely without letting arbitrary host filesystem state silently redefine an Agent's effective behavior.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT managed-root isolation, explicit mode conversion, filtered manifests and recovery warnings. Represent an InstructionBundle as a versioned content-addressed Artifact with manifest, provenance, reviewer/approval, size/type policy and atomic publication; materialize it through Connector/Artifact ports into sandbox-owned directories. Treat arbitrary external roots as local-development imports only, resolving symlinks and scanning content before admission. Disk recovery must produce a proposed reconciliation, not silently supersede authoritative metadata.
units.responsibilityConflict: Instruction content can change Agent behavior and tool usage, yet filesystem copies/recovery have no author, approval, hash, effective interval or link to ResponsibilityContract. Preferring disk over stored metadata can silently activate unreviewed instructions, and external directories may expose unrelated code, credentials or personal files.

units.function: Pure domain-helper tests for deciding whether an Agent can be invoked from its Agent-only reporting chain and enumerating descendants invalidated by a terminated manager.

units.keyDataModels: Agent id/Company/status/reportsTo, manager chain, invalid-org-chain flag, reason code and affected descendant ids.
units.lifecycle: An otherwise active Agent is blocked when any ancestor is terminated, its manager is missing or the reporting graph cycles. Terminating a root identifies all non-terminated descendants whose chain becomes invalid while excluding terminated descendants and unrelated roots.
units.testAssessment: Three focused graph cases cover terminated ancestry, missing nodes, cycles, descendant enumeration and unrelated roots. Missing are cross-Company manager ids, self-loop explicitly, deep-chain performance/stack safety, duplicate ids, non-active intermediate statuses, simultaneous graph updates, mixed human/Agent principals, project responsibility, accepted delegation and reason stability across schema versions.
units.designRationale: Prevent Agents from receiving new assignments or runs when the modeled management hierarchy cannot supply a valid supervisory chain, and surface deterministic repair reasons.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must guarantee every executable Agent role reaches an active accountable human through valid organization/responsibility relations before work is authorized.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure cycle/missing/terminated graph validation and affected-descendant calculation. Generalize the graph to typed Human/Agent positions and ResponsibilityContracts, require termination at an active accountable human, scope every edge by Company and effective interval, version the graph snapshot used for authorization and emit remediation projections without conflating structure with accepted responsibility.

units.function: Large route-level authorization suite spanning Agent read/config redaction, updates, host commands and instruction paths, Agent creation/hiring/approval/termination, runtime defaults, environment compatibility, task-assignment grants, peer configuration, Agent inbox and heartbeat cancellation.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes combine authenticated actor and AccessService decisions with Agent/Approval/Heartbeat/Environment/Secret/Instruction/Skill/Budget services, normalize configuration, persist Agent/membership/grant state and emit ActivityLog/telemetry. Tests mock nearly every service but exercise the real Express route branching.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor and Company scope, Agent adapter/runtime/permissions/trust/status, SecretRef env, host workspace command, InstructionBundle path, Agent membership/grants, hire Approval, heartbeat/model-profile defaults, instance Environment/driver, task-assignment source, peer configuration and user inbox filter.
units.lifecycle: Read-only members receive empty adapter/runtime config while privileged Board views retain full config. Unauthorized members cannot update, create keys or wake Agents. Agent self-service cannot set host commands or instruction roots, including nested cheap profiles and hires; Board administrators can. Direct creation requires agents:create and is disabled when Company hire approval is required, creates membership plus tasks:assign, disables timer/cheap profiles by default and tolerates optional model-profile discovery failure. Pending Agents can be approved directly or through a linked approval; termination resolves linked approval and cancels invocations. Environment drivers are checked against Adapter capability, including instance-scoped cross-Company environments. Permission updates preserve omitted Skill denial but couple Agent creation to task assignment. Peer config reads require suggest/configure grants; cross-tenant Agent/run operations return 404.
units.testAssessment: Forty-plus route cases provide unusually broad regression coverage for sensitive branches, nested command denial, Secret normalization, approval double-apply avoidance, environment/Adapter compatibility, cross-tenant hiding and patch preservation. Missing are production AccessService/database/transaction integration, denial side-effect assertions on every branch, immutable decision receipts, optimistic concurrency, requester-versus-approver separation, Secret redaction even for admins, command allowlisting/sandboxing, revoke/session propagation, risk/data policy, user inbox delegation binding, scoped peer resource checks, environment trust and rollback across Agent/grant/instruction/approval writes. The suite explicitly demonstrates raw API-key return to a privileged Board actor and arbitrary userId in Agent inbox lookup.
units.designRationale: Centralize a complex compatibility surface while preventing Agent self-escalation into host code/filesystem control, supporting simple-mode usability, optional enterprise approval and multiple local/remote runtimes without breaking older configurations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs action-specific, tenant- and resource-scoped authorization that separates human viewing, proposing, approving and executing; no convenience mode may bypass Secret custody, accountable delegation or data-purpose boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT nested dangerous-config detection, read-versus-admin projections, explicit create permission, approval-linked idempotent activation/termination, timer-off defaults, environment capability checks, tri-state patches and cross-tenant 404. REJECT raw Secret values in any config response, arbitrary Board-authored host commands without code-package trust/approval, direct self-approval, simple-mode task assignment and canCreateAgents=>tasks:assign coupling. Bind inbox access to signed delegated-human scope, not a query userId. Split the monolithic route into commands with PolicyPort decisions and immutable receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: A privileged Board response can contain PAPERCLIP_API_KEY plaintext. A Board actor can configure host-executed commands and directly approve a pending Agent without demonstrated separation of duties. Newly created/active Agents receive task assignment broadly, expanding delegation without a ResponsibilityContract. An Agent can request another user's inbox view by userId without a signed on-behalf-of binding. Peer suggest access is decided at Company resource scope rather than the exact target Agent/config fields.

units.function: Unit tests for role-derived Agent permission defaults, normalization of stored overrides and create-versus-patch schema semantics for Agent and Skill creation authority.

units.lifecycle: Only the exact CEO role receives Agent-creation permission by default; explicit overrides win. Every role receives Skill-creation permission by default, including legacy records that omit the field. Full parsing defaults omission to true, while patch parsing preserves omission as unchanged and explicit false remains false.
units.testAssessment: Five concise cases pin intended defaults, override preservation and correct tri-state patch behavior. Missing are unknown/Unicode/case-normalized roles beyond examples, migration impact counts, policy versioning, permission provenance/expiry, deny conditions, separation of duties, Skill risk classes, organization scope and end-to-end enforcement. units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish harmless reusable prompts from executable/tool-bearing Skills and ensure an Agent cannot expand its or peers' effective capabilities through a permissive content-creation default.

Default all effectful capability creation to deny; use explicit versioned grants scoped by tenant/project, Skill risk class, tool/data permissions, expiry and accountable grantor. Preserve the useful omitted-versus-explicit-false patch semantics and run a deliberate migration rather than silently elevating legacy records.
units.responsibilityConflict: Every role, including ordinary Agents, can create a Skill by omission, which may become a durable instruction/tool supply-chain artifact without accountable approval. units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end tests for run-bound Agent Secret metadata/value access, binding resolution, success auditing, runtime log-redaction registration and denial of low-trust/special-scope callers.
units.dependencyDirection: An Agent actor and heartbeat run enter Secret routes; SecretService resolves Agent and run-snapshotted Project bindings, decrypts a local-encrypted version, registers the returned value with the run redaction registry, writes SecretAccessEvent/ActivityLog records and returns metadata or plaintext value.
units.keyDataModels: Company Secret/provider/version, target binding/config path/projection class, Agent/run/key scope, run context manifest and redaction fingerprint/material, SecretAccessEvent and ActivityLog.
units.lifecycle: Listing returns only bound Agent plus run-manifest Project Secret metadata and emits no value-access event. Fetching a bound value returns key/value/version with no-store, first persists a redaction registration without embedding plaintext in the run snapshot, then records success. Concurrent identical registrations deduplicate. Persistence failure rejects delivery. Unbound values are denied. Low-trust review, task-bridge and skill-test callers cannot list or fetch.
units.testAssessment: Four strong database cases cover multiple binding layers, metadata-only listing, plaintext non-leak assertions, success audit, fail-closed redaction, concurrency deduplication and three restricted caller classes. Missing are cross-Company/run/Agent mismatches, revoked/rotated Secret versions, provider outage, lease/TTL/single-use delivery, response/body/log proxy leakage, memory zeroization, denial audit for unbound requests, purpose and data-export policy, high-risk approval, rate limiting, concurrent rotation, KMS/HSM and proof that redaction material itself is encrypted and access-controlled.
units.designRationale: Allow a running Agent to discover only assigned Secrets and fetch values when necessary, while registering exact redaction material before release so subsequent logs can be scrubbed and denying less trusted execution lanes entirely.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret delivery that is tenant-, Work-, Connector-, purpose- and data-policy-bound, keeps values out of the control-plane domain where possible and leaves a complete custody/access record.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT binding resolution, metadata/value separation, no-store, redaction-before-delivery, failure closure, run snapshot manifest and low-trust denial. Prefer execution-node injection or short-lived broker leases over plaintext control-plane API responses; bind every access to WorkExecution, ResponsibilityContract, purpose and export policy, use provider/version references, expiry and least-use scope, and audit allowed plus denied attempts without revealing Secret existence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A successful fetch is linked to Agent/run but not to an accountable human, exact permission/data contract or approval. Plaintext crosses the HTTP/control-plane boundary. An unbound Secret request is denied without a SecretAccessEvent or ActivityLog entry, leaving attempted access outside the responsibility record even if existence-hiding is desired.

units.function: Pure helper tests for normalized Agent display-name collision detection and automatic numeric suffix selection.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService passes an in-memory Agent name/status set to shortname normalization helpers before create/update naming; no database constraint or external dependency is involved.
units.keyDataModels: Agent id/name/status, normalized shortname, excluded Agent id and generated numeric suffix.
units.lifecycle: Active Agents collide after normalization, the Agent being updated is excluded, names with no normalized shortname do not collide and terminated Agents are ignored. Deduplication retains the original name or appends/increments a suffix until the snapshot appears unique.
units.testAssessment: Eight small cases cover normalization, termination, self-exclusion, empty normalized names and suffix progression. Missing are Company scoping, Unicode/confusables/case locale, reserved names, very long values, database uniqueness, concurrent creates, deleted/reactivated Agents, historical reference ambiguity and deterministic behavior under duplicate existing names.
units.designRationale: Keep UI-friendly Agent handles readable and avoid common naming clashes while allowing names from retired Agents to be reused.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs stable human-readable labels without ever using them as identity, authorization or responsibility references, and must preserve clarity across termination/reactivation and imports.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Use immutable opaque Agent/Principal ids and separately scoped, database-constrained slugs with Unicode-confusable policy and optimistic retry. Treat display names as non-unique. Do not automatically reuse a terminated Agent's slug where historical responsibility views could become ambiguous; require an explicit alias lifecycle.
units.responsibilityConflict: Reusing a normalized shortname after termination can make audit exports and human approvals appear to refer to a new Agent when older records used the same label. Snapshot-only suffixing races under concurrent creation and provides no proof of identity continuity.

units.function: Schema compatibility tests for optional provenance/display metadata on Agent Skill entries and legacy snapshots that omit those fields.
units.dependencyDirection: Shared Zod validators parse Adapter-produced Skill entries/snapshots before server routes and Web projections consume them; provenance is descriptive and optional.
units.keyDataModels: Skill key/runtime name, desired/managed/state, Adapter type/mode, origin/origin label/location label/readOnly/detail and warnings.
units.lifecycle: New entries may describe a user-installed external read-only Skill and its filesystem location, while older snapshots without any provenance continue to parse unchanged.

Missing are allowed origin/state transitions, package/version/digest/license/signature, publisher, install time, trust and review status, permission/tool/data manifest, location sanitization, tamper detection, legacy quarantine and whether readOnly is enforced rather than displayed.
units.designRationale: Improve Skill UI transparency without breaking existing Adapter snapshots or forcing all runtimes to provide provenance immediately.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a verifiable Skill/Plugin supply-chain contract that distinguishes desired configuration from installed code and prevents unreviewed instructions/tools from gaining enterprise authority.

units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes authorize and resolve Agent/Company state, use CompanySkillService to canonicalize catalog/version selections, resolve Adapter config through SecretService with user Secrets skipped, delegate list/sync to the active Adapter, persist desired state in Agent adapterConfig and compose AgentService/Instructions/Approval/Issue-link/telemetry flows for creation and hiring.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/Adapter config, desired Skill key or key+versionId, add/remove/replace merge mode, runtime Skill entry/snapshot, beta-Skill setting, user/company Secret context, managed InstructionBundle, pending hire Agent, Approval requestedConfigurationSnapshot and source Issue link.
units.lifecycle: List and sync inspect catalog entries without materializing missing runtime files and skip user-specific Secrets while retaining actor context for company-Secret audit. Sync requires explicit add/remove/replace, canonicalizes references, optionally accepts version pins behind an instance beta flag and persists desired state before Adapter sync. Unknown legacy keys remain visible/removable but are excluded from runtime version selection. Direct creation and hires canonicalize Skills, reject legacy prompt fields, materialize managed default/custom instructions and include desired Skills/config in hire approval payloads.
units.testAssessment: Thirty substantial route cases cover Claude/Codex/ACPX/persistent modes, Secret-resolution options, explicit merge semantics, version gating, stale references, canonicalization, direct create, telemetry role, instruction defaults, legacy rejection and hire approval/source preservation. Missing are real authorization denials and cross-tenant checks, concurrent sync/version conflicts, rollback when persistence or Adapter sync fails, Skill digest/signature/license/trust, permission/tool/data manifests, risk-based approval on post-hire changes, uninstall/rollback, Adapter partial failure, audit events, runtime attestation, malicious Skill content and proof that stale/unverified entries cannot execute through another path. Heavy mocks leave database/filesystem/plugin boundaries unverified.
units.designRationale: Separate desired Skill selection from runtime representation, avoid side effects during reads, preserve backward-compatible stale choices, make destructive replacement explicit and keep Agent creation/approval configuration stable across multiple Adapter ecosystems.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a vendor-neutral Skill/Plugin lifecycle where desired capability, reviewed package version, Connector materialization and effective runtime authority are distinct, auditable states tied to accountable humans and data policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT side-effect-free list/sync preparation, explicit add/remove/replace, canonical references, unresolved-item quarantine, Secret-safe audit context and approval configuration snapshots. Move desired Skills out of vendor Adapter config into a versioned CapabilityAssignment aggregate. Admission requires immutable package digest, provenance/license/signature, declared tools/permissions/data egress and compatibility; activation and every authority-expanding change require risk-based human approval and atomic publish/rollback. Connector-specific materialization remains an Adapter responsibility.
units.responsibilityConflict: A permitted sync can change effective Agent instructions/tools without a new ResponsibilityContract or approval, and a global beta flag substitutes for package trust. versionId is not shown to bind immutable content or license. Stale/unverified keys persist alongside valid desired state. Default instruction bundles encode Paperclip-specific API and operational doctrine, so copying them would couple Company OS behavior and responsibility semantics to a competitor's control plane.

units.function: Route tests for running Adapter environment diagnostics on the explicitly selected sandbox/remote target, managing test leases and merging Environment Secret/plain variables with Agent config.
units.dependencyDirection: The route authorizes Company Adapter configuration, resolves Environment and Secret bindings, acquires/realizes a fresh execution lease, resolves an Adapter execution target, invokes Adapter.testEnvironment with merged config and always releases the driver lease with released/failed status.
units.keyDataModels: Company Environment/driver/config/envVars, SecretRef/missing binding, execution lease/workspace/target, Adapter config env, diagnostic check/status and sandbox/provider/snapshot identity detail.
units.lifecycle: Missing or unsupported requested environments return structured diagnostics without host probing. A supported target uses a fresh non-reused lease with custom image, archives it on release and reports sandbox identity. Workspace failure marks/releases the lease failed. Environment env is the base layer, Agent env wins, protected PAPERCLIP_API_KEY is filtered, and missing Secret bindings add failure checks; however the Adapter probe still runs with remaining variables when a binding is missing.
units.testAssessment: Seven route cases cover the critical no-host-fallback invariant, missing target, happy-path lease identity/release, realization failure, env precedence/protected key filtering and missing-binding diagnostics. Missing are real authorization denials, cross-Company environment id, probe timeout/cancel/network policy, malicious Adapter output, lease cleanup failure, archive retention/privacy, Secret redaction in diagnostic/error/logs, Agent override of protected environment policy, idempotency/rate limits and a fail-before-execute assertion for missing required Secrets.
units.designRationale: Make configuration tests reflect the environment where work will actually run, keep failed sandboxes inspectable and prevent misleading success from probing the control-plane host instead of an unsupported remote target.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a safe Connector/Environment certification probe that never escapes to the host, never runs with an incomplete authority set and produces a structured, attributable health attestation for managed-cloud and local enterprise nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT explicit-target/no-host-fallback, fresh lease, structured diagnostics, protected control-plane keys and release-on-all-paths. Resolve and validate all required Secret/data bindings before executing any probe; apply an allowlisted env merge where policy-owned keys cannot be overridden by Agent config. Run probes in an isolated, egress-limited disposable sandbox and return a signed short-lived HealthAttestation. Archive only after explicit diagnostic-retention policy and Secret scrubbing.
units.responsibilityConflict: A missing required Secret still permits partial probe execution, which can create effects under a different authority set than the approved runtime. Agent config wins env conflicts without shown policy classification. The test action has no accountable requester/approval/audit receipt, and archived failed sandboxes may retain enterprise data or credentials.

Missing are cross-user/cross-Company denial, revoked/rotated values, purpose/expiry, probe output/log redaction, rate limiting, declaration version/digest, approval, value zeroization and consistency: test-environment intentionally bypasses declarations that login requires.
units.designRationale: Support user-owned credentials for interactive setup and runtime login while keeping audit attribution truthful about which system/environment consumed the Secret and avoiding fabricated Agent responsibility.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs consistent purpose-bound delegation of a human's credential to a Connector action; diagnostic endpoints must not obtain broader Secret access than production execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT responsible-user fail-closed behavior and honest consumer/actor attribution. Require a versioned UserSecretGrant for every use, including diagnostics, binding definition/version, consumer, config path, purpose, Work/test command, expiry and accountable human. Prefer execution-node lease injection and redact probe outputs. REJECT owner-by-key implicit resolution without declaration as an enterprise default.

units.function: Database integration test proving pending-hire Agent configuration is service-frozen and activation reapplies the approved configuration snapshot even after direct Agent-row tampering.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService creates/freeze-checks the pending Agent; ApprovalService stores the requested payload and, on approval, applies that payload back through Agent activation and related budget/config persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Pending Agent identity/role/config/runtime/budget/metadata/permissions, hire Approval requester/decision/payload and activated Agent state.
units.lifecycle: Generic Agent and permission updates on a pending Agent return a structured 409 listing frozen fields. Even a direct database change to name/config/runtime/metadata is overwritten when the Approval is approved, restoring the request snapshot and activating the Agent.
units.testAssessment: One high-value integration case covers service mutation denial, permission denial, deliberate database tamper and full snapshot reapplication. Missing are tampering with the Approval payload itself, cryptographic snapshot digest, concurrent decisions, requester/approver separation, partial apply/rollback, Secret version changes, environment/package availability drift, rejection/expiry/cancel and audit evidence linking the exact approved bytes to activation.
units.designRationale: Close the approval-time-of-check/time-of-use gap so an approved hire cannot activate with configuration changed after the reviewer inspected it.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires every high-risk approval to bind the exact action/configuration digest and reject or re-review any drift before execution or Agent activation.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT frozen pending state and snapshot reapplication. Store an immutable canonical request digest plus referenced Instruction/Skill/Secret-policy/Connector versions, sign or hash-chain the decision receipt, enforce requester/approver separation by risk and revalidate dependencies at activation. Any drift creates a new approval revision rather than silently reapplying mutable JSON.
units.responsibilityConflict: The same board-user requests and approves in the fixture, and the mutable Approval payload is treated as authoritative without content digest or independent evidence. units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must let a human acknowledge/remediate a failed Agent without erasing evidence or accidentally resuming stale authority/session state.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret custody and projection contracts that cannot diverge from approved Agent/Connector configuration and that roll back atomically on invalid or unavailable authority.

units.function: HTTP integration tests for the custom API JSON compression middleware, including content negotiation, cache validators, streamed/download responses and Better Auth's writeHead plus Uint8Array response bridge.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes emit responses through an API-scoped middleware that temporarily wraps ServerResponse write/end/flushHeaders, buffers eligible JSON and asynchronously applies node:zlib gzip or deflate before restoring the original methods.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP Accept-Encoding quality preferences, Content-Type/Encoding/Disposition/Range/Cache-Control, ETag and Content-MD5 validators, status/body eligibility, Buffer and Uint8Array chunks, write/end callbacks.
units.lifecycle: A request selects gzip or deflate before route execution. The middleware buffers JSON writes unless headers, streaming semantics or response metadata require passthrough; bodies below 1 KiB remain unchanged, eligible large bodies are compressed and validators adjusted, while compression failure falls back to the original bytes.
units.testAssessment: Ten real-socket tests strongly cover hot-list compression, both encodings, small/already-encoded/streamed/attachment responses, ETag weakening and the Better Auth Uint8Array regression. Missing are malformed and duplicate q-values, q=0 versus wildcard precedence, HEAD/204/304/errors, Cache-Control no-transform, flushHeaders, callback/backpressure ordering, client aborts, compression failure, Content-MD5 removal and a maximum buffered-body or concurrency memory bound.
units.designRationale: Reduce bandwidth on large JSON control-plane reads without corrupting authentication and download responses whose Node response semantics differ from ordinary res.json output.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will return large task, evidence and office projections and needs transport efficiency that preserves identity cookies, evidence bytes, streaming and cache correctness under self-hosted and managed profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the regression corpus and protocol guards, but prefer a maintained platform/proxy compression facility or a bounded implementation. Add Brotli where supported, hard buffer/concurrency limits, abort handling and metrics; never transform evidence downloads or signed/digested payloads unless the stored and transported representations are explicit.
units.responsibilityConflict: Compression is not a responsibility model, but silent byte transformation can invalidate evidence digests or obscure which representation was approved. The middleware buffers eligible JSON without an upper bound, creating a control-plane availability risk that is not exercised by the tests.

units.dependencyDirection: Session or API-key actor middleware supplies trusted human/Agent identity; approval routes scope records to the actor's Company, call Approval/IssueApproval/Heartbeat/Secret/Access services, then emit activity and wakeup side effects only when a decision was newly applied.
units.keyDataModels: Board or Agent actor, Company scope, Approval type/status/payload/decision note/requester/decider, linked Issue ids, heartbeat run contextSnapshot and status-only recovery capability flags.
units.lifecycle: Approve/reject retries return the resolved record without repeating logs, issue lookup or wakeups. Cross-Company decision and revision attempts return indistinguishable 404. Normal Agents may open generic board requests linked to Issues, while cheap status-only recovery runs cannot create, resubmit or comment on approvals.

Missing are requester/approver separation, role/risk policy, exact action and payload digest binding, evidence/result/permission/data-contract references, concurrent requests, Idempotency-Key, revision versioning, comment/list/read containment, expired/cancelled approvals, structured error codes and real database/service integration rather than permissive mocks.
units.designRationale: Keep retries safe, derive attribution from trusted authentication context, avoid tenant existence oracles, let Agents escalate decisions to humans and prevent degraded watchdog runs from changing governance state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Agent-initiated escalation and human decisions that are tenant-safe and retryable while proving the exact proposed action, authority, data, evidence and accountable human through revision and execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT actor-derived attribution, 404 non-disclosure, explicit low-trust capability denial and issue/work linkage. Replace generic title payloads with a versioned ApprovalRequest binding canonical action digest, Work, ResponsibilityContract, Agent, permission/data grants, evidence and expiry; require policy-selected accountable human and structured stable errors.
units.responsibilityConflict: An Agent can create a generic board approval whose fixture binds only a title and optional Issue ids, not an executable action or responsibility contract. Human decision tests prove identity attribution but not authority, independence, what the reviewer saw, or whether later side effects match the approved bytes.

units.function: ApprovalService unit tests for compare-and-set decision idempotency, hire-Agent activation/creation side effects and lookup of an Agent's open hire approval.
units.dependencyDirection: ApprovalService reads and conditionally updates Approval rows, then invokes AgentService activation/create/terminate and an external hire-approved notification hook; a SQL-filtered query finds open hire approvals by Company, type, status and payload Agent id.
units.keyDataModels: Hire Approval company/type/status/payload/requesting Agent, decision user/note/time, optional pending Agent id, Adapter config SecretRef, applied boolean and post-decision Agent/notification side effects.
units.lifecycle: A pending approval is conditionally resolved. If another worker wins, the service rereads the final row and returns applied=false without repeating Agent or notification effects. A winning approval activates the pending Agent or creates one from payload and notifies the requester; rejection terminates the pending Agent. Open-hire lookup delegates all predicates to SQL.
units.testAssessment: Six focused service tests demonstrate the compare-and-set winner/loser contract, winning side effects, Agent creation from SecretRef payload and filtered lookup. The database and downstream services are stubs, so they do not cover transaction isolation, crashes between status update and side effects, side-effect failure/retry, outbox durability, duplicate external notification, concurrent payload mutation, approval digest, create/activate rollback, requester/approver policy or JSON predicate/index behavior.
units.designRationale: Prevent concurrent or retried decisions from activating, terminating or notifying twice while supporting both pre-created pending Agents and deferred creation from an approved payload.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must resolve approvals exactly once at the decision ledger while guaranteeing eventual, idempotent execution of every approved side effect and preserving proof that execution used the approved revision.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the boundary around an immutable decision plus transactional outbox/work command. Keep conditional state transition and explicit applied result, but persist a canonical action digest and durable side-effect intents in the same transaction; consumers use idempotency keys, retry independently, record execution receipts and compensate or escalate permanent failure.
units.responsibilityConflict: The current no-op retry rule creates a crash gap: if the database becomes approved and Agent activation or notification fails, later retries see applied=false and deliberately skip those side effects. Approval payload JSON is mutable authority without an immutable digest, and the tests do not prove that the exact reviewed configuration is what an external runtime receives.

General assets admit configured non-image attachments; logos require supported images, use the general size ceiling and sanitize SVG scripts, event handlers and external links before storage. units.function: Pure tests for configurable attachment MIME allowlists, wildcard matching, content-type normalization, Office-type inference from filenames and the set of content types eligible for inline browser rendering.
units.dependencyDirection: Operator configuration and upload metadata enter normalization/matching helpers; routes use their result to admit uploads and choose inline versus download behavior, independent of storage or domain services.
units.keyDataModels: MIME type/pattern, wildcard, default allowlist, original filename/extension, octet-stream fallback, inferred Office MIME type and inline-safe content-type set.
units.lifecycle: Missing allowlist configuration falls back to images plus common Office types. Matching is case-insensitive and supports type or suffix wildcards and a global *. Generic binary uploads may be relabeled as Office documents from filename extension when the inferred type is allowed. PNG/SVG/PDF/plain text/MP4 are classified inline; HTML and ZIP are not.
units.testAssessment: Twenty-one concise cases cover parsing, normalization, wildcard behavior, legacy/current Office extensions, generic binary inference and inline classification. Missing are MIME parameters, malformed patterns, Unicode/double extensions, magic-byte or archive inspection, macro-enabled Office types, polyglots, decompression bombs, executable content, SVG/PDF active-content behavior, browser nosniff/CSP/sandbox/Content-Disposition and the danger of the global allow-all wildcard.
units.designRationale: Accept useful office and media attachments across inconsistent clients while retaining configurable admission and preventing obviously active or binary types from inline rendering.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS evidence and enterprise-data uploads are untrusted inputs whose admission, rendering, model ingestion and export must be governed separately and preserve the original bytes and declared/detected representations.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT normalization and table-driven parsing only. Do not treat client MIME or filename inference as trust; record declared, detected and normalized types, hash original bytes, quarantine and scan asynchronously, validate archives, enforce per-purpose policy and serve active formats from an isolated origin with nosniff, sandbox and attachment disposition. Disallow unrestricted * in managed production profiles.
units.responsibilityConflict: A filename can cause generic bytes to be relabeled as an Office document and several active-capable formats are called inline-safe without proving delivery controls. That weakens evidence integrity and can expose accountable reviewers when opening Agent-supplied artifacts.
